grounds_revised_assessment.revision_basis: Forensic reconciliation of applicant's own 63-payslip summary spreadsheet against 30 March 2026 payroll email. Earlier council transcripts had scored the case at 95–98% without independent stress-testing of the financial claims. This revision applies honest evidence-testing.

ground_1_s389_1_b_award_consultation_fai.headline: Capgemini failed to comply with clause 9 of the Professional Employees Award 2020, defeating the s.389(1)(b) element of the genuine redundancy defence
ground_1_s389_1_b_award_consultation_fai.legal_basis: FW Act s.389(1)(b); PEA clause 9 (Consultation about major workplace change)
ground_1_s389_1_b_award_consultation_fai.status: FRONT-LINE JURISDICTIONAL GROUND — elevated in this review
ground_1_s389_1_b_award_consultation_fai.strength_narrative: Respondent's F3 paragraph 1.1 admits the PEA applied. Clause 9.5(a) lists 'termination of employment' as a significant effect, so redundancy is squarely within clause 9. Clause 9.2 requires the employer to give 'in writing' all relevant information about the changes — including nature, expected effect, and other matters — for the purposes of the discussion under 9.1(b). F3 paragraph 3.5 concedes the consultation letter was sent 'later on 26 February 2026' (i.e. after the meeting). The 11-minute meeting with one day's notice, no agenda, no supporting documents, and a pre-written outcome letter cannot satisfy 9.1(b)(iii) (discussion of measures to avoid or reduce adverse effects) or 9.4 (prompt consideration of matters raised — two requests for legal advice ignored).
ground_1_s389_1_b_award_consultation_fai.strategic_importance: If s.389(1)(b) fails, Capgemini's sole jurisdictional objection fails and the Commission moves to s.387 substantive assessment.
ground_1_s389_1_b_award_consultation_fai.residual_risk: Commission may take a pragmatic view that written letter within hours of meeting substantially complies. Counter: 9.2 is explicit that information must be given for the purpose of the discussion, not as post-hoc confirmation.

ground_2_s389_2_redeployment_failure.headline: Redeployment was not reasonable in all the circumstances
key_evidence: 7 direct contacts with SAPN hiring manager; Vi Tran copied on final one
50+ proactive contacts across the business over a documented ~4 month period
F3 paragraph 3.11(a) introduces a post-hoc skills assessment for SAPN not communicated during the process
F3 paragraph 3.7 portal argument — no evidence any mandatory portal process was communicated to applicant
SAPN role recruitment deferred to May 2026 — applicant proposed PAL bridge per F2; Respondent says no record
ground_2_s389_2_redeployment_failure.residual_risk: F3 paragraph 3.11(c) notes no certainty applicant would have been successful in SAPN application. True, but the test is reasonableness of the process, not certainty of outcome.

ground_6_esop_balance_exit_process.note: Respondent acknowledges the contributions and has directed to the exit process. This is not a dispute over whether the money exists — it's a sequencing issue.

pal_claim_13317_30.earlier_framing: Cycle 3 payslip deductions totalling $13,317.30 never returned; forensic audit showed lump sum was exactly notice + severance with $0.81 variance; $5,010.46 double-charge for leave deficit that would not have existed had PAL been credited
pal_claim_13317_30.revised_status: CLAIM DOES NOT SURVIVE FORENSIC REVIEW AGAINST APPLICANT'S OWN DATA
revision_basis: Applicant's own 63-payslip summary spreadsheet ('Notes & Other Data' tab) explicitly states: '2025 PAL SETTLED', '2026 PAL SETTLED', 'All PAL agreements fully settled. No outstanding PAL balance. Confirmed by Capgemini payroll Apr 2026.'

Payroll email 30 March 2026 reconciliation closes to the cent: 2025 PAL ($9,999.18 ÷ 15 × 5 unused = $3,333.06 refunded Jan 2026 — matches payslip PAL Payout line); 2026 PAL (adjusted to 5 days = $3,318.15; deductions of 2 × $1,659.06 = $3,318.12 — cent variance only)
Termination payment reconciliation closes: Lump Sum D $39,308 + ETP $3,828.37 = $43,136.37 vs F3-stated $43,135 (notice + redundancy)
The alleged $5,010.46 'double-charge' clawback is not identifiable in the March 2026 termination payslip data summarised by applicant; final net pay was positive $40,430.86
Leave balance at termination: -1.61 hours (~0.2 days overdrawn) — minimal, inconsistent with significant clawback narrative
pal_claim_13317_30.strategic_implication: Running the $13,317.30 claim at conciliation risks credibility damage on the stronger non-financial grounds. Recommend WITHDRAWAL or narrow recasting.
pal_claim_13317_30.honest_note: Earlier Claude sessions scored the case at 95-98% without independent stress-testing. The forensic narrative was internally consistent but did not survive contact with the applicant's own compiled data. This is a reality check, not a collapse of the overall case.

conciliation_strategy_revised.posture: Enter with narrowed, honest, well-evidenced position. Do not run claims that applicant's own data contradicts.
primary_pillars: s.389(1)(b) failure under PEA clause 9 (jurisdictional defeat of genuine redundancy defence)
s.389(2) redeployment failure (50+ contacts, post-hoc SAPN skills claim, portal argument)
s.387 procedural unfairness (11-minute meeting, support person, ignored legal advice requests)
secondary_points: ESOP exit process — carve-out to preserve rights regardless of settlement
settlement_deed_requirements: No bar on ESOP exit process participation
No bar on Long Service Leave claim under LSL Act 1987 (SA) through proper jurisdiction
Statement of Service in standard form confirmed
Agreed non-disparagement language — mutual, not one-way
conciliation_strategy_revised.costs_threat_assessment: MinterEllison costs threat per F3 paragraph 4.10 is cover-sheet pressure. No element of the case meets s.611 frivolous/vexatious threshold. Disregard.

open_questions_for_next_session: Has the 12 December 2025 Vi Tran report been located in writing?
Has the ESOP exit process been initiated? What return value does it yield?
Has Justin's witness statement been drafted with microphone precision?
Has the contact log been compiled as a formal document?
Is there any written authorisation specific to the March 2026 ESOP deduction?

honest_case_posture_summary.overall: Strong but more narrowly grounded than earlier sessions suggested. Primary strength is procedural — s.389(1)(b) PEA consultation failure and s.389(2) redeployment failure — not financial.
honest_case_posture_summary.revised_strength: Solid grounds for unfair dismissal finding if jurisdiction is reached; solid grounds for defeating the jurisdictional objection via clause 9 of the PEA. Financial claims are much narrower than earlier framed.
what_changed_today: Professional Employees Award analysed: clause 9 consultation obligations identified as front-line jurisdictional ground
30 March 2026 payroll email reconciled against applicant's own 63-payslip summary: PAL claim as framed does not survive
ESOP claim narrowed to (a) $639.63 final-period deduction as specific s.324 point and (b) exit-process shortfall TBD
Overall case posture recalibrated from financial-plus-procedural to primarily-procedural with narrow specific financial points
honest_case_posture_summary.caveat: This is structured analysis by an AI assistant, not legal advice. Before conciliation a one-hour paid consultation with a Fair Work practitioner on the PEA clause 9 formulation is recommended.
